title: Why Pen Caps Have a Hole
topic: The hole in many pen caps is a safety vent (ISO 11540); the barrel hole balances pressure

beats.narration: Look at the top of your pen cap.
beats.caption: LOOK AT THE CAP
beats.direction: Urgent, playful command, like grabbing a friend's attention. Hit 'Look' and 'top'.

beats.narration: That tiny hole isn't mainly for the ink.
beats.caption: NOT FOR THE INK
beats.direction: Lower, conspiratorial, a knowing twist. Lean on 'isn't'.

beats.narration: It's there in case you inhale the cap.
beats.caption: IN CASE YOU INHALE IT
beats.direction: Serious but calm, a reveal. Slight pause before 'inhale'.

beats.narration: Kids chew caps, and sometimes one slips into the windpipe.
beats.caption: INTO THE WINDPIPE

beats.narration: One study of forty-four children found most needed a procedure under anaesthesia.
beats.caption: 44 CHILDREN
beats.direction: Measured, factual, give the number weight.

beats.narration: So in 1990, Britain wrote a safety rule for pen caps.
beats.direction: Storyteller mode, curious, a turn in the story.

beats.narration: BIC vented its caps, and took the idea worldwide.
beats.caption: WORLDWIDE

beats.narration: Today's standard asks for at least eight litres of air a minute.
beats.caption: 8 LITRES A MINUTE

beats.narration: Enough to keep some air flowing until help arrives.
beats.caption: UNTIL HELP ARRIVES

beats.narration: So which hole actually helps the ink?
beats.caption: WHICH HOLE?
beats.direction: Playful question, rising intonation, set up a twist.

beats.narration: The tiny one on the side of the pen.
beats.caption: THE SIDE

beats.narration: If someone's choking, call emergency services right away.
beats.caption: CALL FOR HELP
beats.direction: Clear, firm and caring, a public-service tone.

beats.narration: Send this to someone who chews every pen they touch.
beats.caption: SEND THIS TO A PEN CHEWER
beats.direction: Friendly, direct to camera, playful and a little teasing, like you're nudging the viewer to share. Smile in the voice.
